subject: Clarify: SCC mappings + UK Addendum — auditable subprocessor chain
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@wellbridgehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@wellbridgehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: SCC mappings + UK Addendum — auditable subprocessor chain

Hi Ellen / team,

Thanks again for the quick review on the DPA. A couple of points came up internally after reading your checklist:

- Your security team asked that we provide a per-region mapping that shows which SCC variant applies (EU SCCs vs. UK IDTA + Addendum) per processing activity and per subprocessor — effectively a dual-mapping table.
- You also requested an "auditable chain" for subprocessors that records when subprocessors start/stop processing and the legal basis used for each transfer (SCC vs. IDTA).

I've attached an initial SCC_Dual_Mapping_Proposal_v1.pdf that sketches how we can map endpoints and subprocessors to the appropriate transfer mechanism and include a timestamped record for each change. High level proposal:
  * We keep canonical mapping files per-account in a Drive folder (exportable CSV)
  * Each mapping update is stapled to an audit event (who changed it, when, reason)
  * We expose an evidence package for customers: subprocessor inventory, routing logs (sampled) and signed mapping snapshot for the relevant date range

Before I loop infra/legal in, two asks so we can tailor the package:
1) Do you need a signed attestation for each mapping snapshot (DocuSign)?
2) What retention window do you need for audit events (6/12/24 months)?

Proposed next step: 30-minute evidence-sprint call next week with your security + procurement, and our infra + legal. Let me know available slots.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[attachment: SCC_Dual_Mapping_Proposal_v1.pdf]

From: Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@wellbridgehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@wellbridgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarify: SCC mappings + UK Addendum — auditable subprocessor chain

Logan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposal. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Signed attestation per snapshot: Preferred, yes. We need a cryptographic proof or DocuSign signature attached to the CSV snapshot that shows it was the authoritative mapping on a given date.
- Retention for audit events: 24 months for production data. For pre-prod we can consider 12 months.
- Routing logs: we don't need full request bodies — metadata is fine (timestamp, route tag, model id, egress region, subprocessor id). We will request a sampling strategy during the call.

One red flag from our Security team: they want evidence that Redwood supports an on-prem fallback for a narrow set of workflows in case of cross-border restriction (we call these "edge-only" flows). Is on-prem fallback feasible for those?

I attached our wellbridge-compliance-checklist.xlsx — it lists the exact evidence items we need. Please review and highlight any items you can't provide.

Available for a call next Tue/Wed morning UK time.

Best,
Ellen Cho
Head of Security — Wellbridge Health
[attachment: wellbridge-compliance-checklist.xlsx]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@wellbridgehealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: SCC mappings + UK Addendum — auditable subprocessor chain

Hi Ellen / Logan — adding technical context from Infra/Platform: 

- Routing & logs: We can emit per-request routing metadata that includes a route_tag, region_hint, selected_model_variant, and subprocessor_id. We plan to make a sampled export (configurable by account) that matches the fields in your checklist. See attached routing-snippets.txt for field examples.
- On-prem fallback: For "edge-only" flows we support two modes:
    1) VPC-private deployment: customer-run instance (we can provide a Private artifact + deployment manifest) — suitable for long-term on-prem requirements.
    2) Short-term evacuation / reroute: we can route traffic to a UK-only cluster and pin model variants to onshore storage for the duration. This is not strictly "on-prem" but can satisfy data residency if combined with contractual constraints.
- SCC vs IDTA: The runtime does not change behaviour based on the legal instrument; mapping is a metadata layer. We can snapshot the mapping and cryptographically sign the CSV using our signing key and add DocuSign if you prefer a human-signature layer.

Known limitation: We cannot currently produce egress packet captures (pcaps) for legal reasons — all evidence will be metadata + logs + signed artifacts.

If this matches what you need we can prepare a 2-week evidence sprint plan and list deliverables.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

[attachment: routing-snippets.txt]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@wellbridgehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Draft DPA amendment language + timeline

Ellen / team — attaching a redline that adds two paragraphs to the DPA to support the dual-mapping and auditable chain requirements. Key clauses in the draft: 

1) Mapping snapshot clause (new): "Provider shall maintain a dated mapping of Processing Activities to Transfer Mechanisms (SCCs / UK IDTA / other lawful basis). Provider will produce a signed CSV snapshot on request for the prior 24 months."
2) Subprocessor event trail (new): "Provider will record subprocessor engagement events (onboard/offboard/change) and provide an export with timestamps and the legal basis for each transfer)."
3) Evidence sprint & SLA: We propose a 10-business-day SLA for initial evidence packaging after request; full 2-week sprint if integration is required.

Open legal items for your review: customer-supplied KMS vs provider-managed encryption keys (affects evidence packaging), and whether DocuSign signature is required for each snapshot or acceptable as a quarterly attestation.

Laura — can you confirm whether the provider-managed KMS flow will allow us to produce the signed snapshots without material changes?

I'll wait for your notes and then push the redline to procurement/legal for Wellbridge.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

[attachment: dpa-amendment-draft-redline.docx]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@wellbridgehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@wellbridgehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: SCC mappings + UK Addendum — auditable subprocessor chain

Ellen — thanks for the checklist and the availability. Quick summary and proposed next steps so we have an auditable trail of decisions: 

- Evidence package: Redwood will produce a signed CSV snapshot, sampled routing metadata (configurable), and subprocessor event trail exports covering 24 months for production.
- Signature: We'll support both cryptographic signing (machine-signed snapshot) and DocuSign for human attestation. Please confirm which you prefer for the first snapshot.
- On-prem fallback: Kimberly's note above outlines two viable options. If you need true customer-run on-prem we can prepare a Private deployment plan, but that will add time to delivery.
- Timeline: Proposed 2-week evidence sprint starting Apr 9. Deliverables: signed snapshot, sample routing export, subprocessor CSV, sprint notes and reproduction steps.

Proposed meeting: Tue Apr 10 10:00–10:30 UK time — Infra (Kim), Legal (Priyom), and Privacy (Logan) + your Security/Procurement. I'll send an invite once you confirm.

If that works, we'll start preparing the Drive folder and HubSpot record (linked).

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[attachments: SCC_Dual_Mapping_Proposal_v1.pdf, routing-snippets.txt, dpa-amendment-draft-redline.docx]
